input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: After stripping ANSI codes the prompt text is also passed through str.strip(), which removes the whitespace at the end of the prompt that separates it from the user's typed input.
- failure path: click.prompt("Name") builds the prompt 'Name: '; when the stream does not support color (piped output, CliRunner, NO_COLOR) the prompt is shown as 'Name:' with the cursor glued to the colon, while on a color-capable terminal the same call keeps the trailing space, so transcripts differ between the two environments.

Reviewer finding
- description: When ANSI stripping is triggered, the code calls `.strip()` on the whole prompt text after `strip_ansi`. This removes leading and trailing whitespace, including the trailing space in prompts such as 'Name: ' and any intentional leading indentation.
- rationale: Trigger: a prompt is shown on a non-tty stream or under CliRunner, where `should_strip_ansi` returns True. `strip_ansi(text).strip()` then turns 'Name: ' into 'Name:', so the user's input is typed right against the colon. `echo` strips only ANSI codes and keeps whitespace, so prompt output differs between tty and non-tty streams. Tests that compare prompt output also break.
critique: The finding pins the cause on the `.strip()` call made after `strip_ansi` when color is unsupported, which removes the trailing space in 'Name: '. It also describes the same tty/non-tty difference as the label, so it is the same mechanism.
